ranked_facts.why: positive reactivity to melanocytic markers HMB45, MITF2, and Melan-A is strongly indicative of Malignant Melanoma of the Caruncle
solid tumor with an inflamed crust on its surface, composed of large anaplastic cells with mitotic activity is more typical of Malignant Melanoma of the Caruncle

fact_rationales.F10: The high proliferative index indicated by Ki-67 staining is more typical of malignant melanoma, but can also be seen in other aggressive carcinomas.
fact_rationales.F4: The presence of an amelanotic, pedunculated mass with an ulcerated surface is more typical of malignant melanoma, but can also be seen in other carcinomas.
fact_rationales.F8: The microscopic examination showing a solid tumor with anaplastic cells and mitotic activity is highly suggestive of malignant melanoma, and less typical of squamous or basal cell carcinoma.
fact_rationales.F9: The positive reactivity to melanocytic markers is highly specific for melanoma, making it strong evidence for FLAT.1 and against FLAT.2 and FLAT.3.
